name: Alberti (proper)
description: low-high-mid-high, the bass note RE-ARTICULATED, not a held drone: `A2e E3e C3e E3e A2e E3e C3e E3e`. Light, transparent. Best for lyrical themes. Don't run it for more than ~4 bars unbroken.
shorthand: A2e E3e C3e E3e A2e E3e C3e E3e

name: Oom-pah (the Classical default, lighter than Alberti)
description: bass on beats 1 & 3, chord on 2 & 4: `D2q [D3,F3,A3]q A2q [D3,F3,A3]q`. The single most idiomatic Classical accompaniment. Bass LEAPS between root and fifth; the off-beat chord is mid-register.

name: Oom-pah-pah / waltz-feel in 4
description: bass then two chords: `D2e [F3,A3]e [F3,A3]e ...`

name: Broken / murky octaves (Sturm und Drang motor)
description: the D-minor storm engine, alternating octave tremolo: `D2s D3s D2s D3s ...` or `D2e D3e D2e D3e D2e D3e D2e D3e`. Use for dramatic, driving passages — this is what K.466 uses, NOT static-pedal Alberti.

name: Repeated chords (pulsing)
description: `[D3,F3,A3]e` ×8, or quarter pulses. Gives weight without melodic figuration. Good under a busy RH.

name: Walking / scalar bass
description: quarter or eighth notes stepping through the harmony: `D2q E2q F2q G2q` — drives transitions and sequences.

name: Sustained / held
description: LH holds a chord or octave for the whole bar while the RH carries everything: `[D2,D3]w` or `[D3,A3,D4]w`. ESSENTIAL for breathing — use it where the RH is active or at a phrase peak.

name: Unison / octave doubling with RH
description: both hands strike the same line for a bare, dramatic tutti stroke (theme statements, climaxes): LH mirrors the RH an octave or two below.

name: LH rest / drop-out
description: the LH is SILENT for a beat or a bar (rest), letting the RH ring or breathe. Mozart uses silence constantly. A `rest` in the LH is not a bug.

name: Two-voice / contrapuntal bass
description: a real melodic line in the LH answering the RH (varied recaps, developments).

name: Alberti bass
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Murky bass (octave alternation)
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Waltz bass (3/4, L:1/8)
when_to_use: Simple support (stay out of melody's way)

name: Rachmaninoff wide-span
density_suggestion: Sixteenth notes throughout; Dense sixteenths or heavy chords; Maximum density or massive chords

name: Scalar fill ascending
density_suggestion: Sixteenth notes begin; Sixteenth notes throughout

name: Tremolo
density_suggestion: Dense sixteenths or heavy chords; Maximum density or massive chords

name: Chordal with passing tones
density_suggestion: Sixteenth notes; Sixteenth notes throughout; Dense sixteenths or heavy chords

name: Parallel thirds & sixths
description: the signature Mozart sweetness for lyrical themes. Double the melody a 3rd or 6th below in the same rhythm: `[F5,A5]q [E5,G5]e [D5,F5]e ...`. Use across lyrical second themes and consoling passages. Don't overuse in stormy material.

name: Appoggiatura "sigh"
description: a dissonance ON the strong beat resolving DOWN by step on the weak beat, slurred two-note: `(G5q F5q)` over an F chord (the G leans, the F resolves). The emotional core of Mozart's minor-key writing. Place at phrase peaks and cadential approaches.

name: Cadential trill
description: a trill on scale-degree 2 (or the dominant note) approaching a PAC, ideally with a turned suffix: `A5h:tr` then resolve to the tonic. Reserve for real cadences (PAC, important HC), not every bar.

name: Turns & mordents
description: a gruppetto (turn) wrapping a sustained melody note `:turn`, a mordent `:mord` on an accented note. Ornament arrivals and long notes, not running passages.

name: Grace-note appoggiatura
description: a short `:grace` note leaning into a strong beat from a step above. Adds vocal inflection at phrase starts/peaks.

name: Echo dynamics (terraced repetition)
description: state a 1-2 bar idea `f`, then immediately repeat it (often an octave up or same register) `p`. A quintessential Mozart/Classical gesture. Great for presentation phrases and codettas. Mark the dynamics explicitly.

name: Triplet contrast
description: break prevailing duple (eighths/sixteenths) with a bar or two of triplet figuration for rhythmic variety and forward lilt.

name: Scale flourish as punctuation
description: a fast run is connective/cadential tissue, used ONCE to drive into an arrival — not the default surface. If a phrase is >55% stepwise, replace some runs with arpeggios/leaps.

name: Leap-to-peak then step-down
description: approach a registral apex by leap (6th, octave, arpeggio), then release it by step. Gives the line a profile and a clear high point.

name: Periodic structure
description: antecedent (4 bars, ends on a HC, "question") + consequent (4 bars, begins like the antecedent, ends PAC, "answer"). Make the consequent's opening RECOGNIZABLY echo the antecedent.

name: Sentence structure
description: presentation (a 2-bar basic idea + its repetition, often sequenced up a step or varied) → continuation (fragment the idea, accelerate harmonic rhythm) → cadence. Mozart's primary themes are often sentences.

name: Deceptive feint
description: approach the cadence, then resolve V→vi instead of V→I once, before finally landing the real PAC. Adds a moment of surprise.

name: Cadential 6/4
description: at important cadences: I6/4 → V(7) → I. Lean the 6/4 on a strong beat (it's a dominant-function suspension).

name: Feminine cadence
description: resolve the final tonic on a WEAK beat (e.g. beat 2), often after an appoggiatura. Gentler than a downbeat slam; very Mozart for lyrical endings.

name: Neapolitan (bII6)
description: in minor, a flat-supertonic-sixth chord for a dark expressive stab before the dominant. Let it land (fp, slight hold).
